processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with the nominal composition Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%) were produced by melting raw materials with high purity (>99.9 %) using a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
Homogenized ingots were hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates were cut into 10×5×2 mm³ samples using electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq: samples were solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching.
Solution-treated samples were aged at temperatures between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h, followed by water quenching. This sample corresponds to the 550 °C / 10 h condition (15Al).

structures.overall_structure: After aging the 15Al alloy's α matrix transforms to β-Mn. At 550 °C the α→β-Mn transformation is almost complete after 6 h (only scarce α remains) with a new fine BCC phase formed within the β-Mn; by 10 h the aged structure is essentially a uniform β-Mn matrix containing fine new precipitates.

phases_present.morphology: essentially uniform matrix after near-complete α→β-Mn transformation
fine new phase / elongated red network within the β-Mn, resolved only at high magnification

precipitates.distribution: within the β-Mn matrix; resolved as fine dot-like precipitates in the 550 °C−10 h SE-SEM panel

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase
interfaces.interface_notes: The β-Mn is an Mn-rich phase; its nucleation/growth enriches Mn while expelling Fe, Al and Cu toward the surrounding matrix, which drives formation of the BCC (Al-enriched) and FCC Cu-rich phases at the β-Mn interfaces. The precipitates between β-Mn interfaces increase with Al content.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s on an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester; each sample repeatedly tested 5 times and the value given as the average of 5 measurements.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N, dwell 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the solution-treated and aged samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 15Al sample aged at 550 °C for 10 h reached 961.1 ± 19.6 HV (Table 2).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases such as α-Mn and β-Mn in the aged 15Al samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 15Al alloy aged at 550 °C − 10 h the SE-SEM panel shows a uniform (essentially fully transformed β-Mn) matrix with a 10 µm inset marked by magenta 'New precipitates' arrows.

unmapped_findings: The 15Al alloy aged at 550 °C for 10 h gives a Vickers hardness of 961.1 ± 19.6 HV (Table 2), the second highest hardness among all 15Al aging conditions, just below the global 15Al maximum of 965.6 ± 7.6 HV obtained at 600 °C/6 h.

For the 15Al alloy the α→β-Mn transformation at 550 °C is nearly complete after 6 h (Fig 4b), and by 10 h the SE-SEM structure is a uniform β-Mn matrix with fine new precipitates (Fig 7, 550 °C − 10 h panel).

The 15Al alloy density measured by the Archimedes method is 6.85 g·cm^-3 (b0017); the reported ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g corresponds to the peak-hardness 15Al condition (Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu), not explicitly to the 550 °C/10 h condition.

The 15Al alloy shows the fastest β-Mn precipitation kinetics: within 3 h of aging at 525 °C the α matrix was almost completely transformed into β-Mn, and at 550 °C this near-complete transformation occurred within about 6 h, versus 6 h (17Al) and 10 h (19Al) at 550 °C for the higher-Al alloys.

Reported nanoindentation hardness (11.7 ± 0.4 GPa) and intrinsic β-Mn hardness (12.1 ± 0.3 GPa) for 15Al were measured on the hardest sample (600 °C/6 h, 965.6 HV), not on the 550 °C/10 h condition, so they are not assigned to this sample.
